case_title: State of Maharashtra v. Pankaj Jagshi Gangar
statutory_provisions: IPC s.384, s.386, s.387 r/w. s.34; Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act s.23(1)(a) and s.21(4)
aggravating_circumstances: Running Matka business; providing funds to international gangster and his gangs; arranging funds for purchasing weapons and information; active member of organized crime syndicate
offence_finally_established: Offences under Sections 384, 386, 387 read with Section 34 of the IPC
neutral_facts: The accused was involved in running a Matka business and was providing funds to an international gangster and his gangs. The investigating agency found that the accused was arranging funds for the expenses of purchasing weapons and information and was an active member of an organized crime syndicate. A charge sheet was filed against the accused under the IPC and the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act. The accused applied for bail before the Special Judge, which was rejected. The accused then filed a bail application before the High Court, which was heard by a Single Judge, who was not inclined to grant bail. The accused withdrew the application and filed a writ petition before the Division Bench of the High Court, which granted interim relief by releasing the accused on bail. The Supreme Court quashed the High Court's order and directed the accused to surrender and face trial.
